purpose: Compare synthetic read-only OTIO-style and ffprobe-style media representations without mistaking partial metadata for a complete editorial timeline.

activities.label: normalize OTIO-style and ffprobe-style payloads through the shared CloudEvents and media contract
attack source identity ranges markers timebase editorial completeness and write boundaries
record which representation semantics are portable and which require a sidecar

queries.expression: does an OTIO-style payload preserve timeline range marker and audio video sync semantics
which media asset stream codec and timebase facts are available from a ffprobe-style payload
does missing editorial data produce PARTIAL_UNKNOWN instead of fabricated timeline claims
does the bridge reuse the shared CloudEvents identity provenance replay and read-only kernel

assumptions: Both representations are synthetic payloads modeled after documented fields, not tool output captured from a file.
The media timeline contract from experiment 072 is the target normalized representation.
A stream report cannot be treated as an editorial timeline without a separate authorized source.
Read-only normalization is reversible and does not imply playback or export permission.
This comparison must not install tools or decode media.
kill_tests: An OTIO asset hash mismatch blocks normalization.
An OTIO source range outside available range blocks normalization.
An OTIO marker without source frame blocks normalization.
Missing ffprobe streams blocks the representation.
An invalid ffprobe timebase blocks the representation.
A ffprobe payload cannot claim editorial completeness without timeline fields.
Cross-representation asset identity mismatch blocks comparison.
A writable bridge policy blocks the adapter.
A missing OTIO representation blocks the comparison.
A missing required event blocks the shared envelope.
unknowns: Whether a real OTIO adapter needs transitions, effects, nested stacks or time warps beyond this fixture.
Whether ffprobe metadata plus a real sidecar can provide stable linkage under file replacement.
Whether VFR, drop-frame and keyframe semantics need a versioned media contract extension.
Whether rights and player capability can be independently verified in a live system.
